primitives.summary: A boxed monospace label in a semantic colour, like a sticker on the board. It names a thing, a state or a result in two or three words ("429", "CACHE HIT", "RATE LIMITED").
primitives.whenToUse: Labelling a state, outcome or status code; calling out the key term of the beat; marking a result as ok or problem. `reject` turns it red with a cross.
primitives.whenNotToUse: Sentences or explanations (the narration and headline carry those); numbers that change (use `counter`); a component or service in a system diagram.

text.description: Short label, shown in uppercase monospace.

semantic.description: Colour meaning: neutral label, focus, ok, problem or concept.

primitives.summary: A big number with an optional unit and caption. It shows `from` until a `count` event, then counts up or down to `value`, so the viewer watches a quantity grow or drain.
primitives.whenToUse: One quantity that matters to the story: requests per second, tokens left, queue length, latency. Use `count` when the change itself is the point.
primitives.whenNotToUse: A word or status instead of a quantity (use `tag`); a countdown in time; several numbers at once (one counter per number, and only the ones the story needs).

value.description: The number shown once any count has finished.

from.description: Shown until a `count` event, which then counts to `value`. Set it whenever you use `count`.

semantic.description: Colour of the number: neutral, focus, ok, problem or concept.
